It trips the prose Global Constraint "No file outside a task's own Files block is edited" — a constraint with no `Check:` behind it, so this is minor, not blocking, and nothing about it endangers the Claim: every Machine clause is already settled by the driver's `Run:` evidence at exit 0.

Two things make it worth deleting rather than keeping. (a) It is a second exam file on the surface the peer's graded exam already covers — its own docstring says so ("the implementer's copy of the same contract, kept under a different name so the two never collide"), and its RUN_BULLETS list is the task's `Run:` commands transcribed verbatim. That is precisely the shape the sentence this same diff adds to §The six body slots forbids: "Name one exam file per behaviour surface... a later task on that surface... extends that file instead of opening a second one." Committing it makes the repo contradict the rule the patch just wrote, and its name (`..._implementer_check`) is a task-noun name rather than a surface name. (b) `test_m5_the_tests_that_read_the_skill_still_pass` shells out to a nested `pytest` over eight test files that the committed suite (the stated acceptance mode) already runs, roughly doubling their cost on every suite run and re-reporting their failures under this file's name.

completenessFindings.detail: Global Constraint "No file outside a task's own Files block is edited" is unmet: the integrated tree carries two test files that no task's Files block names. Task 1's Files block is `Modify: skills/ultralearn/references/distilling-proposals.md` and nothing else; Task 2's is `Modify: skills/ultrawrite/SKILL.md` and nothing else, and the plan's Parallelization rationale states "Neither task creates a test file: each deliverable is prose and proves itself with `Run:` commands." Present anyway: `tests/test_ultrawrite_surface_rules_implementer_check.py`, whose own docstring self-identifies it as "Implementer's own red/green check for Task 2 (#609 items 1 and 3, #665 (a))" and re-runs Task 2's nine `Run:` greps plus its M5 checks through `bash -c`; and `tests/test_spec_review_brief_selfcheck.py`, which regex-pins Task 1's rewritten §The spec review section (its `HEADING = "## The spec review (spec approval — every spec in this repo)"` and its assertion at line 123 that "Historical specs carry `## Trim review` sections" are Task 1's M1/M4 greps verbatim). Neither file can predate the run: the first names this run's Task 2, and the second asserts a heading that BASE (4bd0f5c) did not carry — at BASE the section was `## The trim review`, per Task 1's Context. Both are committed into the suite the driver ran, so they are durable, not scratch.

Doctrine and artifact disagree on the same literal rule, in one tree. Task 2's deliverable `skills/ultrawrite/SKILL.md` says at lines 92–93 "A task whose deliverable is prose proves itself with `Run:` commands, never with a test that matches sentences of a document" and repeats it in §Self-review at lines 340–341 ("No Proof pins a sentence of a document as its evidence; a prose task's Proof is a `Run:`"); `CLAUDE.md` §How features are built here (lines 234–238) records the same rule as settled, with the 224 prose-pin tests in 25 files deleted in the lift. The two files named in the previous finding are that species: `tests/test_spec_review_brief_selfcheck.py` matches sentences of `skills/ultralearn/references/distilling-proposals.md` by regex over the section text (lines 59–123), and `tests/test_ultrawrite_surface_rules_implementer_check.py` does the same to `skills/ultrawrite/SKILL.md` through shelled-out greps. Both tasks' Context slots also grant that "the phrases inside the greps are the contract, the wording around them is yours" — a licence the committed pins now revoke for the next author, who will break the suite by rewording prose the plan said was theirs. Same two files as the blocking finding; the remedy is the same removal.

Cross-document literal now stale: `CLAUDE.md` line 232 points readers at "(dispatch brief still in `skills/ultralearn/references/distilling-proposals.md` §Trim review)", but Task 1's M1 deleted that heading — the file's section is now `## The spec review (spec approval — every spec in this repo)` (line 119) and no heading beginning `## The trim review` remains. Task 1's Context anticipated the CLAUDE.md relationship only for historical specs' own sections, and the brief keeps that sentence (line 158, "Historical specs carry `## Trim review` sections under this brief's former name"), so the retained half is correct; what is stale is CLAUDE.md's anchor to the brief's own section name. `CLAUDE.md` is outside Task 1's Files block and the Global Constraint forbids editing it, so the implementer was right not to touch it — this is a follow-up issue, not a defect in the task's diff. The path in the pointer still resolves; only the section anchor is wrong.
